editor_note: Entries 9-10 are faithful and natural: "Primitivas" heading, the little-endian/`big` default contrast kept intact, and "las primitivas Sampler y Estimator del IBM® Quantum Compute Service devuelven resultados big-endian, pero Executor devuelve resultados little-endian" preserves the exact endianness split.

The seven rewritten headings are faithful and match each other, using infinitives throughout: "Monitorear, calibrar y evaluar con benchmarks", "Monitorear parámetros", "Monitorear de forma holística", "Calibrar" and "Evaluar con benchmarks". They also fit the body text's "monitoreo"/"benchmarking", so nothing needs changing.

Entries 5-11 are faithful and read naturally in tú register, for example "caracterización del ruido cuántico basada en aleatorización", "ZNE con gate-folding, así como postselección para filtrar errores no markovianos" and "Fermi-Hubbard en 1 y 2 dimensiones", with nothing dropped or distorted.

The six rewritten entries keep the English meaning, and the product and category names (Qiskit Functions, Circuit function, Application function) correctly stay in English. The problem is that entries 7, 8 and 9 leave ordinary nouns in English inside Spanish sentences: "circuit"/"circuits" ("la lógica original del circuit", "circuits dinámicos", "a mitad de circuit", "síntesis de circuits") and "gates" ("gates de dos qubits", "gates SWAP"). Older entries on the same page (69, 74) use "circuito", so the page is now inconsistent. The meaning holds throughout. The negations, quantities and caveats are all faithful, including the gamma/acceptance trade-off, the bias caveat and the 5,000/8,334 shot arithmetic, so nothing here would mislead a learner. What needs fixing is consistency within the file. "spacetime" appears as both "espaciotemporales" and "espacio-temporales", and "coherent Pauli checks" as both "comprobaciones coherentes de Pauli" and "comprobaciones de Pauli coherentes". Other split pairs are costo/coste, autovalor/valor propio, palabras de código/palabras código, and "ancilla" switches between masculine and feminine (los/las ancillas, un/una ancilla). Two individual phrasings should also change: the 2.1 heading uses "filtración" (usually read as "leak") where the rest of the file says "filtrado", and "descartamos las ejecuciones que afectaron" in [6] is ambiguous about who affected whom.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the subtle parts: TREX removing bias while adding variance, ZNE assuming rather than guaranteeing well-behaved scaling, the PEC/ZNE incompatibility and the 30-qubit PEC result being worse than unmitigated. I found no drift. The remaining problems are consistency only. "shots" is masculine in most of the file ("muchos shots", "cada shot") but feminine in [405]–[407] ("todas estas shots", "Las shots individuales", "Algunas shots"). "Overhead" is rendered as both "sobrecarga" and "sobrecoste", and "quasi-probability" as both "cuasiprobabilidades" and "cuasi-probabilidad". Decimal separators also switch between the comma ("54,5 %", "0,5 %") and the point ("2.9%", "86.4%", "0.959"). Smaller slips include "bitstrings" in [159], where every other entry has "cadenas de bits", and the awkward "el modelo de ruido es de Pauli-twirling" in [419].

The meaning is faithful throughout. I found no drift: the negations hold, the bound direction is right ("cota superior variacional", "monótona no creciente"), and the angle-magnitude argument in [170] and the M_J/product-stage reasoning all match the source. The problems are term inconsistencies that start partway through the file. "shot" appears as "medición" ([21], [28]), "disparo" ([73], [103], [109]) and the English "shot" ([136], [144], [170], [176]). "hamiltoniano" switches to "Hamiltoniano" from [131]. "SQD agrupada" switches to "SQD agrupado" ([157], [170], [173]). "complemento SQD" becomes "addon SQD" ([149], [150]), "cuaderno" becomes "notebook" in [156], and "auxiliares" becomes "asistentes" in [162]. "conjunto" is used for both the excitation pool and the circuit ensemble, which produces the clumsy "Repartir el conjunto entre un *conjunto* de circuitos" in [73].

examples.translation: Este tutorial se presenta como un notebook de Python con fines didácticos.
examples.suggested: Este tutorial se presenta como un cuaderno de Python con fines didácticos.
examples.why: Entry [1] translates the same phrase as 'cuaderno de Python'. Using both renderings in one file is inconsistent.

editor_note: Entry 18 is faithful and keeps the caveat: "Hasta que lo hagas, la celda no guarda nada, así que ejecutar todas las celdas nunca puede sobrescribir una cuenta que hayas guardado antes" matches the English, and the step references (paso 4/paso 5) and informal tú ("ejecuta", "Reemplaza") are correct.

None of the three rewritten titles would mislead a learner, and entry 37 ("Tomografía de sombras del estado de Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger") is clean. Entry 23, "Optimización multiobjetivo aproximada cuántica", copies the English adjective order, so "cuántica" ends up dangling after "aproximada". A native editor would write "Optimización cuántica aproximada multiobjetivo", which also matches how entry 20 handles QAOA ("optimización aproximada", with "cuántico" attached to the head noun). Entry 38 turns the English imperative "Simulate" into the noun "Simulación", while the sibling titles 29, 30, 61 and 62 all use the imperative "Simula".

examples.source: Quantum approximate multi-objective optimization
examples.translation: Optimización multiobjetivo aproximada cuántica
examples.suggested: Optimización cuántica aproximada multiobjetivo
examples.why: Copying the English adjective order leaves 'cuántica' tacked on at the end. Spanish puts 'cuántica' right after the head noun, as entry 20 does with 'Algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada'.

examples.source: Simulate time evolution of the transverse-field Ising model
examples.translation: Simulación de la evolución temporal del modelo de Ising de campo transversal
examples.suggested: Simula la evolución temporal del modelo de Ising de campo transversal
examples.why: The English uses the imperative 'Simulate', and the other 'Simulate ...' titles on this page use 'Simula' (entries 29, 30, 61, 62). The noun form 'Simulación' breaks that pattern; the meaning is unchanged.

editor_note: The rewritten Fortran entries are faithful. The key claims all carry over correctly: the -40.472331 MeV lower bound in 204, the rule that per-step mode is the only option for saved bitstrings in 209, the discard-versus-repair caveat in 221 and the mass-rescaling warning in 226. The problems are surface-level. Entry 182 leaves the English word 'circuit' where it should say 'circuito'. 'Shots' is 'shot' in 182 (and in the Python section) but 'mediciones' in 192, 213 and 220. 'Bindings' is left as 'bindings' in 170 but translated as 'enlaces' in 198 and 199, which is ambiguous next to 'enlazado'. 'Build' in 174 is the calque 'construcción' where it should be 'compilación'. Smaller points: Hamiltoniano/hamiltoniano capitalization is mixed, the Fortran learning outcomes switch to infinitives ('Construir', 'Filtrar') next to an imperative 'Aprende', and the thousands are written '4,096' instead of 4096.

examples.source: Noise changes *which* determinants the circuit proposes
examples.translation: El ruido cambia *qué* determinantes propone el circuit
examples.suggested: El ruido cambia *qué* determinantes propone el circuito
examples.why: An untranslated English word (or a truncated one) is left in the Spanish sentence.

examples.source: Keep only shots with the right proton number...
examples.translation: Conserva solo las mediciones con el número correcto de protones...
examples.suggested: Conserva solo los shots con el número correcto de protones...
examples.why: Entry 182 and the whole Python section say 'shots', but entries 192, 213 and 220 say 'mediciones'. The term should be the same throughout the page.

examples.source: the Fortran bindings for Qiskit
examples.translation: los enlaces de Fortran para Qiskit
examples.suggested: los bindings de Fortran para Qiskit
examples.why: Entry 170 keeps 'bindings'. 'Enlaces' reads as hyperlinks, especially since 'enlazado' appears in the same sentence.

examples.source: Check the build locally against an exact reference
examples.translation: Comprobar la construcción localmente con una referencia exacta antes de enviar jobs
examples.suggested: Comprueba la compilación en local con una referencia exacta antes de enviar trabajos
examples.why: In software, 'build' is 'compilación', not 'construcción'. 'Jobs' should be 'trabajos', as on the rest of the page. The other learning outcomes use the imperative, not the infinitive.

examples.source: each with 4,096 shots
examples.translation: cada uno con 4,096 mediciones
examples.suggested: cada uno con 4096 shots
examples.why: Spanish does not use a comma as the thousands separator; entry 123 already writes 4000.

editor_note: I checked the three rewritten entries (18, 65, 71) against the English, and none of them would mislead a learner. They are faithful and use the informal register: "Lee más", "consulta", "Ten en cuenta". Terms match the rest of the page: "antirruido", "paso de transpilación", "cajas anotadas", "encajonar circuitos", and "Qiskit Runtime" stays in English. The one thing a native editor would change is in entry 71: "como resultado de cómo se captura el orden de los qubits" copies the English "as a result of how" word for word and reads stiffly. "debido a la forma en que se captura…" would sound more natural.

examples.source: as a result of how qubit order is captured when boxing circuits and finding unique instructions
examples.translation: como resultado de cómo se captura el orden de los qubits al encajonar circuitos y encontrar instrucciones únicas
examples.suggested: debido a la forma en que se captura el orden de los qubits al encajonar los circuitos y buscar las instrucciones únicas
examples.why: "como resultado de cómo" copies the English construction word for word and reads stiffly. "debido a la forma en que" is the natural Spanish connector here, and the meaning does not change.

editor_note: Entry 126 is faithful and reads naturally: "mapear estos términos de Pauli a la forma canónica esperada por el `Executor`" and "ordenamiento canónico de qubits" match the English, "mapear" is used the same way as elsewhere on the page, and the link text uses informal "visita".

The meaning is faithful throughout, including the caveats that matter: random sampling performs about as well as QAOA at 40 assets ([21], [55]), the 8-asset run is effectively brute force ([43]), and portfolios are always scored against the full objectives ([49]). Terminology is consistent: frente de Pareto, mezclador XY, posselección, Sampler, hamiltonianos. One wording needs a fix. Entry [48] has a gender-agreement error, "Hacer dispersa el modelo de riesgo", where "el modelo" calls for "disperso". "Dispersar el modelo de riesgo" would read better. A smaller point: in [36], "esté 'activo'" (for "on") collides with "activos" meaning assets in the same sentence.

examples.source: **Sparsify the risk model to fit hardware.**
examples.translation: **Hacer dispersa el modelo de riesgo para ajustarlo al hardware.**
examples.suggested: **Dispersar el modelo de riesgo para ajustarlo al hardware.**
examples.why: Gender-agreement error: 'dispersa' does not agree with the masculine 'el modelo'. A native editor would fix it straight away.

examples.source: rotate each qubit so it is "on" with probability $K/N$. Restricted to the $K$-asset outcomes
examples.translation: rotamos cada qubit para que esté "activo" con probabilidad $K/N$. Restringido a los resultados con $K$ activos
examples.suggested: rotamos cada qubit para que esté "encendido" (en 1) con probabilidad $K/N$
examples.why: 'activo' (on) sits right next to 'activos' (assets), so a reader may stumble over the two meanings. It does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the 3^k/4^k sample-complexity caveat, the ancilla bit-flip logic and the postselection-on-0 condition. Nothing would mislead a learner. From about entry [67] on, the page reads as if a second translator took over and term choices split. The core term "shadow" goes from "tomografía de sombras" / "sombras de Pauli" (entries [0] to [59]) to untranslated "tomografía de shadow" / "estimador de shadow" ([67], [72], [75], [82], [86]). Other terms split the same way: "instantáneas" becomes "snapshots", "puertas" becomes "compuertas", "sobrecoste" becomes "overhead", "códigos espaciotemporales" becomes "códigos de espacio-tiempo", and "layout" ([51]) sits beside "disposición" ([75], [80]). There are also small slips: "una sola shot" (gender) and "5,000" with an English thousands separator.

examples.source: The shot scaling of shadow tomography is assessed by plotting...
examples.translation: El escalado de shots de la tomografía de shadow se evalúa graficando...
examples.suggested: El escalado de shots de la tomografía de sombras se evalúa graficando...
examples.why: The first half of the page uses 'tomografía de sombras' consistently. Switching to the untranslated 'shadow' midway breaks the core term.

examples.source: Define the shadow estimator ... used to collect the shadow snapshots.
examples.translation: Define el estimador de shadow ... para recopilar los snapshots de shadow.
examples.suggested: Define el estimador de sombras ... para recopilar las instantáneas de sombras.
examples.why: Entry [17] introduced 'instantánea clásica' for snapshot. Here and in later entries it becomes the English 'snapshots'.

examples.source: gate and readout errors accumulate across the deep GHZ circuit
examples.translation: los errores de compuertas y de lectura se acumulan a lo largo del profundo circuito GHZ
examples.suggested: los errores de puertas y de lectura se acumulan a lo largo del circuito GHZ profundo
examples.why: Entries [30], [34] and [51] use 'puertas'. Entries [75], [80] and [82] switch to 'compuertas'. The phrase 'del profundo circuito' is also an unnatural adjective order.

examples.source: use low-overhead error detection with spacetime codes
examples.translation: usa detección de errores de bajo overhead con códigos de espacio-tiempo
examples.suggested: usa detección de errores de bajo sobrecoste con códigos espaciotemporales
examples.why: Entries [8] and [12] already set 'de bajo sobrecoste' and 'códigos espaciotemporales'. This entry and [90] use different renderings for the same concept.

examples.source: reduces the variance of a single-shot estimate of an observable
examples.translation: reduce la varianza de una estimación de un observable con una sola shot
examples.suggested: reduce la varianza de la estimación de un observable a partir de un solo shot
examples.why: 'shot' is masculine everywhere else in the file ('un número de shots'). 'una sola shot' is a gender slip.

editor_note: The 86 rewritten entries carry the meaning over accurately. The C++ tab's numbers and caveats all survive: 1137 of 10000 shots (about 11%), 49 of 120 α-determinants, 0.1373 Ha above FCI, and the "not controlled" comparison caveat. None of these entries would mislead a learner. The problems are term consistency with the rest of the page. The rewritten C++ entries say "cadenas de bits", but the unchanged Python tab says "bitstrings" (entries 87, 97, 98), so the comparison table and entry 163 use a different word for the same thing the Python tab describes. The rewritten entry 136 also says "puertas X" while the Python tab's entry 69 says "compuertas X". Entry 132 is also clumsy because it uses "conjunto" for both the operator "sets" and the circuit "ensemble" in a single sentence.

examples.source: Bad-symmetry bitstrings
examples.translation: Cadenas de bits con mala simetría
examples.suggested: Use one term for 'bitstrings' across the page: either align the rewritten C++ entries with the Python tab's 'bitstrings', or change the Python tab to 'cadenas de bits'
examples.why: The table contrasts the C++ tab with the Python tab, but the Python tab calls the same objects 'bitstrings' (entries 87, 97, 98), so the term changes between the two tabs.

examples.source: applying X gates to qubits 0-6 and 10-16
examples.translation: aplicando puertas X a los qubits 0-6 y 10-16
examples.suggested: Use the same word for 'gate' everywhere on the page ('puertas' or 'compuertas')
examples.why: Entry 69 in the Python tab describes the same Hartree-Fock preparation with 'compuertas X', so the two tabs use different words for the same gates.

examples.source: Draws the operator sets for 100 random circuits ... The next step turns these sets into the ensemble of qDRIFT circuits.
examples.translation: Extrae los conjuntos de operadores ... El siguiente paso convierte estos conjuntos en el conjunto de circuitos qDRIFT.
examples.suggested: El siguiente paso convierte estos conjuntos en el ensamble (o la colección) de circuitos qDRIFT.
examples.why: Using 'conjunto' for both 'sets' and 'ensemble' in one sentence reads awkwardly and blurs the difference between the two.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the end of the page: the δt trade-off in [63] and [67] (finest step has the smallest Trotter error but worse agreement) and the reference caveat in [64] both survive intact. Two terms are used inconsistently within the file. "Trotterized" is rendered as "trotterizada" in [15] but as the longer "con descomposición de Trotter" in [40], [41], [46] and [67]. "Notebook" is "cuaderno" in [22] and [25] but stays "notebook" in [36]. Neither would mislead a learner; core terms such as qubit, puerta, valores esperados, transpilar, magnetización alternada and red tensorial are correct and consistent.

examples.source: in the notebook or Julia REPL
examples.translation: en el notebook o en el REPL de Julia
examples.suggested: en el cuaderno o en el REPL de Julia
examples.why: Elsewhere in the file (entries 22 and 25) it is 'cuaderno'; this should match.

examples.source: Small-scale simulation of the Trotterized circuits
examples.translation: Simulación a pequeña escala de los circuitos con descomposición de Trotter
examples.suggested: Simulación a pequeña escala de los circuitos trotterizados
examples.why: Entry 15 uses 'trotterizada'. The file switches between that and the longer paraphrase; choosing one form would make it consistent and less wordy.
